sections.title: Replay and comparison
sections.what: Rebuilds the facts and project outcomes from the saved stages, runs the routing, and prints the comparison and a sample of facts still unrouted.
sections.why: Shows whether the new routing leaves fewer facts unrouted than the old one.
sections.watch_out: Percentages divide by the number of admitted facts, which gives a meaningless result if that count is zero.

summary: Replays a newer routing rule on a saved Lessons Learnt run and compares the result with what the run actually used, without saving anything.
purpose: Lets the team test a routing change against real past data before adopting it.
why: Likely reason: a read-only comparison lets the owner judge a change safely.
how: Reads the saved stage results for one run, adds outcomes, relevance and verification results to each fact, runs the new routing, then prints the before and after counts of routed and unrouted facts, plus a sample of unrouted facts.
inputs: An optional run id on the command line. A default run id is built in.
outputs: A JSON comparison and a sample list printed to the screen.
risks: Read-only. The built-in default run id means running with no argument always uses that one run. A missing stage result will cause an error.
debug: If a value shows as undefined, that stage was not saved for this run. Check the stage names in the stage results table.
